sentences.text: Public Prosecutor for the State respondent No. 1.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there is no demand of dowry and the FIR does not disclose the allegation of demand of dowry articles.
In the FIR it is mentioned that the incident took place in the night and the petitioner attempted to assault the respondent No. 2.
As a result of which a case under Section 498-A has been registered.
It is also his submission that as there was no demand of dowry, Section 498A IPC is not attracted here in this case.

Accordingly, learned counsel prays to stay further proceedings of G.R. Case No. 14790/2020 (Corresponding to PRC Case No.
1376/2021).
In support of his contention, the learned counsel for the petitioner has cited one case law Manju Ram Kalita vs. State of Assam, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 330.

entities.text: Manju Ram Kalita vs. State of Assam, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 330
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned Addl. Public Prosecutor has fairly submitted that there is no allegation of demand of dowry in the FIR and Section 489A is not attracted in this case.

Considering the submission of the learned counsel for the parties, further proceedings of G.R. Case No. 14790/2020 (Corresponding to PRC Case No. 1376/2021) pending in the court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kamrup (M), Guwahati is hereby stayed till the next returnable date.
Issue notice to the respondent No. 2.
The petitioner shall take steps for service of notice upon the respondent No. 2 by registered post with A/D as well as by usual process, returnable within Page No.# 3/3 4 weeks.
List the matter accordingly after 4 weeks.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
